Subject: Request: standby RTO tolerance for us-west failover

Marissa,

Thanks for the productive demo yesterday. BlueWave is preparing to move a portion of our throughput into Redwood Dedicated (us-west). One operational ask came up from our platform team: during a regional failover into us-west we need a longer standby activation window for stateful caches and warming of in-memory indices.

Current language in the draft MSA assumes a 10-minute RTO for cross-region failover. Given our cache footprint and the time needed to rehydrate several large caches and warm GPU-backed model shards, we need to propose a 30-minute RTO and an RPO of 15 minutes for the initial 90-day cutover.

Would Redwood consider a temporary SLA exception for that environment? We can accept additional runbook-driven checks and agreed pre-warm windows for scheduled switchovers. Our security and compliance teams will also want auditability for each failover event.

Appreciate a quick confirmation so we can finalize the timeline.

Best,
Anna Stewart
VP, Platform Engineering
BlueWave Financial

Marissa / team — technical assessment below. TL;DR: 30-minute RTO for a Dedicated us-west pool is achievable with conditions; there are trade-offs to call out.

What causes the longer activation time:
- Large in-memory KV caches (several TB) that we currently populate lazily. Full rehydration is the dominant cost.
- GPU shard warming (model weights / KV cache priming) for latency-sensitive endpoints that rely on warmed attention caches.
- DNS propagation plus load balancer health checks add 1–3 minutes but are small relative to cache warming.

Mitigations we can require in the amendment:
- Pre-warm window: BlueWave schedules a 30-minute pre-warm during off-peak before any planned failover. Redwood will run a warm-up job that pre-populates the most critical caches.
- Conditional routing: initial traffic shift to a 10% canary for 5–10 minutes to observe error and latency metrics before ramping.
- KV snapshot policy: enable frequent asynchronous snapshots with a 15-minute max age to meet the RPO target.
- Operational readiness: require documented runbook drills every week during the 90-day window. Redwood will provide a runbook template (see DR-runbook-summary.xlsx).

Risks / observable impacts:
- Latency spike risk during the first 10–20 minutes of traffic ramp if caches are not fully warmed. We can reduce this via smarter priming jobs but not eliminate it entirely.
- Increased cost: warm-standby capacity and snapshot frequency will increase run costs; need to confirm who absorbs that.

If Legal signs off on audit and liability language, and Sales accepts the commercial terms, I see no technical blocker to a limited-time exception.

—Dylan
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Marissa / team — security & compliance check:

Auditability requirements:
- Full immutable event log for any failover initiation (who/when/trigger) retained for 365 days.
- Snapshot and KV metadata must be logged to support RPO attestations.
- All cross-region traffic during failover must be TLS 1.2+ and encrypted at rest using customer-managed KMS keys (we can integrate with BlueWave's KMS).

Controls we want in the SLA amendment:
- Redwood to provide access to failover event logs within 48 hours of request.
- A defined post-mortem template and 72-hour logistics window for BlueWave to request additional audit artifacts.

From a compliance standpoint, if BlueWave is using customer-managed keys and we're limiting the exception to a named dedicated pool, this is acceptable. We'll need Legal to sign off on the log access and retention language.

-Neha
Director, Security & Compliance

Proposed limited exception (summary):
- Duration: 90-day exception starting at BlueWave production cutover date.
- RTO: 30 minutes (standby activation window) for the named Dedicated us-west pool.
- RPO: 15 minutes backed by asynchronous KV snapshots.
- Operational requirements: weekly runbook drills in the 90-day window, pre-warm window for any planned failovers, and canary traffic staging during switches.
- Audit & security: 365-day immutable failover event logs, KMS integration allowed, access to logs within 48 hours on request.
- Commercial: Redwood requests a temporary premium to cover warm-standby costs; Karthik will propose the credit structure separately.

If BlueWave agrees to the terms above, Redwood will prepare a short amendment to the MSA (SLA-draft-bluewave-v2.pdf) and share a DocuSign link for signatures. We can also schedule a short runbook walk-through with SRE (Dylan) this week.
